statement: There is a fixed exponent η ∈ (0, 1/8) with the following property. Let µ be a pure critical Gibbs law with common pins, let q = q(σS) be order-positive and centered for its source marginal, and let J be an admissible cut at scales w, s. For every bounded target observable h = h(σT ), when w is sufficiently large, |Eµ[qh]| ≤ C ∥h∥∞ (w/s)−7/8+η Eµ[qMJ ], MJ = s−7/8 ∑ x∈J σx. (2.1) The constant depends only on the admissibility constants and the fixed chart geometry. It is independent of the mass of q+, the mesh, the number and values of source pins, and the ratio w/s. The same inequality holds for expectation differences of two ordered source configurations, and after averaging an ordered coupling of random source configurations, with the common Gibbs continuation. All changed pins and fields lie on the source side of the cut; the target-side continuation is identical in the compared laws. One may decrease η, keeping it positive.
